title: CHECK, UNIQUE & defaults (advanced)
summary: Put business rules where every writer must obey them.
body:
Put business rules where every writer must obey them.

Why it matters: App-side validation protects one code path. Constraints protect the data from every path — scripts, other services, a psql session, a buggy migration.

SQL ↔ ORM: SQLAlchemy CheckConstraint/UniqueConstraint in __table_args__. Prisma @@unique([a, b]), @default(...); CHECK via a SQL migration. SQL: CHECK (...), UNIQUE (a, b), DEFAULT.
why: App-side validation protects one code path. Constraints protect the data from every path — scripts, other services, a psql session, a buggy migration.
objectives: Use composite UNIQUE for 'one per parent' rules.
Know what Prisma can and cannot express (no CHECK — use a SQL migration).
pitfalls: A global UNIQUE where the rule is per parent.
Unnamed constraints — error messages become cryptic.
mappingNotes: SQLAlchemy CheckConstraint/UniqueConstraint in __table_args__. Prisma @@unique([a, b]), @default(...); CHECK via a SQL migration. SQL: CHECK (...), UNIQUE (a, b), DEFAULT.
teachAlong: Cause: Put business rules where every writer must obey them.
Effect: run the exercise and read the gate's rule ids.

exercise.prompt: Add CHECK (price >= 0) and CHECK (stock >= 0) to lab_l14_products.
exercise.hint: Column-level CHECK (…) or a table-level CONSTRAINT name CHECK (…).

wrongSolutions.label: no CHECKs
CHECK (price > -100) — still allows negatives

probes.message: A normal product (stock defaulting to 0) must be accepted.

sql: INSERT INTO lab_l14_products (sku, price, stock) VALUES ('A-2', -1, 1)
probes.message: A negative price must be rejected by the database.

sql: INSERT INTO lab_l14_products (sku, price, stock) VALUES ('A-3', 1, -5)
probes.message: Negative stock must be rejected by the database.
